sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and file purpose
sections.what: Brings in the project and evidence data types, the required field list, the evidence picker, and the empty-value check from the scan fields file. The header comment explains the file's purpose.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps one shared definition of required fields so this report and the scan itself agree.

sections.name: ScanFieldStat
sections.title: Gap count for one field
sections.what: Describes one required field and how many projects are missing its value and how many are missing its evidence.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the report a fixed shape that the screen can read directly.

sections.name: ProjectScanMissing
sections.title: Gap list for one project
sections.what: Holds one project's id and name, the names of the fields it lacks values for, and the names of the fields it lacks evidence for.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the screen say exactly what each project still needs.

sections.name: IndustryScanReadiness
sections.title: Readiness for one industry
sections.what: Groups results for one industry: its name, its project count, the per-field counts, and the projects that still have gaps.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets each industry be shown and checked on its own.

sections.name: ScanReadinessReport
sections.title: Whole readiness report shape
sections.what: The full package returned to the caller: when it was made, which fields were checked, and each industry's results keyed by industry name.
sections.why: Likely reason: one fixed package keeps the caller simple.

sections.name: buildScanReadiness
sections.title: Building the readiness report
sections.what: Walks through every project, sorts it into its industry, and tallies each required field as missing a value, missing evidence, or both. Only projects with at least one gap are added to their industry list. Returns the finished report with the current time.
sections.why: Likely reason: the gate exists to show what is still missing, so it lists gaps and never invents values.
sections.watch_out: The per-field counts depend on each field's position in the shared list, so changing that list order changes which count is which.

summary: Checks every project in each industry for required scan fields that are missing a value or missing supporting evidence, and returns counts and per-project lists without changing any data.
purpose: Shows analysts which projects are not yet ready for a scan, grouped by industry, so they know what to fix first.
why: The file header says it is read-only and must not make up values, so it only reports gaps. The reason for grouping by industry is not stated beyond the header.
how: First it reads the list of required field names from the shared field list in the scan fields file. Then, for each project, it places the project in its industry group. For each required field it checks whether the project has a value and whether usable evidence exists, and records each gap in per-field counts and in a per-project list. Projects with no gaps are left out. Finally it adds the current time and returns the report.
inputs: A list of projects, and an optional map from project id to that project's evidence rows. Each project supplies its id, name, and industry.
outputs: A report with a generation time, the list of required field names, and an object keyed by industry name. Each industry shows its project count, per-field counts of missing values and missing evidence, and the list of projects that have gaps.
risks: A project with an empty or odd industry name creates its own group. The report has no size limit. Evidence is matched by project id, so a wrong id makes every field look as if evidence is missing.
debug: If a project is missing from the report but should show gaps, confirm it has at least one missing value or evidence row. If every field shows missing evidence, check that the evidence map uses the same ids as the projects. For rules about what counts as a value, read the scan fields file.
